$meta.name: TMT balance defaults (measured corpus heuristics)
$meta.source: TMT-Reference/09-Layer-Design-Patterns.md, §4 Balance heuristics table (measured over 132 published games / 770+ layers); some rows cite §2 patterns P1–P17 for detail
$meta.usage: Use these as DEFAULT numbers when filling the design brief and generating code. The Stage-2 self-check and Stage-6 balance walkthrough verify generated numbers against these ranges. A deviation is allowed only when written down in the design brief with a reason (theme ceiling, idle-first pacing, or scope).
$meta.version: 1.2.0 (2026-10-03, phases ⑧ + handbook 12 — added corpusBaselines and authorPacingTargets)

corpusBaselines._source: Full numeric archive of 329 real TMT games (36,111,909 bytes): 1,156 layers, 29,141 component entities, every entry traceable to file+line. Full guide: E:\Idle-Skill\archive\TMT_生成式AI增量游戏数值设计指南.md. These are DESCRIPTIVE baselines for judging whether generated content looks like real TMT content — not prescriptive targets.

corpus.note: challenges are only 1.8% of all components — the component mass is upgrades + milestones + achievements. A generator that splits types evenly does not look like a real game.

layerDensity.note: REPLACES the old qualitative '10+ upgrades + 3-5 milestones' floor with a measured distribution. The 486-component layer is a top-0.1% outlier, not a model.

rowDistribution.note: long decaying tail = the prestige-rhythm curve. Flat layer counts per row read as a flat game.

exponent.note: 0.5 / 1 / 2 dominate; 386 layers omit the field entirely (tab/side layers).

requiresForm.note: 41% of layers gate on a plain literal.

upgradeCost.note: Half of real upgrade costs are hand-written constants; only 10.6% are exponential. Cost ladders in real layers span 6+ orders of magnitude (worked example: c0v1d layer 's' runs 5e3 -> Decimal.pow(10, 545766), with a deliberate cheap 'key' upgrade at 7). A pure geometric ladder is NOT the real shape — and a cost drop is a legitimate rhythm device, not a bug.

upgradeEffects.note: THE headline finding: 54.4% of real upgrades carry NO effect() — their power is wired into the layer's gainMult()/gainExp()/passiveGeneration(), which branch on the upgrade being owned. An effect() nobody reads is a lie; it renders in effectDisplay() and changes nothing. Static rule N-UNWIRED. Also: power/log shapes outnumber plain multiplies ~3:1, so an all-times(2) layer looks unfinished (D-EFFECTSHAPE).

softcaps.typicalForm: a constant that an upgrade later raises, e.g. softcap(){ let C = new Decimal("e1.8e12"); if (hasUpgrade('x', 14)) C = new Decimal("e30000000000003"); return C }
softcaps.note: Only 6% of layers define one — but they are what keep the late game from exploding. The default is: set a LOW constant cap and sell the raise as an upgrade.

gridLayouts.note: Grid shape is pacing, not decoration: a 5x5 upgrade block reads very differently from a 1x3 buyable strip.

buyables.note: Let the engine price buyables via cost_base/cost_mult. Hand-writing 90% of buyable cost functions re-implements the engine and makes them harder to balance.

engineFieldFacts.challengesRepeatableField: completionLimit (number; engine defaults it to 1 — js/technical/layerSupport.js:109-110; 374 real uses)
engineFieldFacts.layerAchievementCondition: done() — condition() is never evaluated (0 of 3,032 real achievements use it)
engineFieldFacts.standaloneNote: addBuyable/addClickable/addAchievement/addGrid/addBar are called 0 times across 329 real games — components are inlined in addLayer().
engineFieldFacts.caveat: Absence in the corpus proves a field is UNUSED, never that it is UNSUPPORTED. Field legality must be checked against references/core/04 and the engine source; corpus is for convention, not validity.

firstMilestone.example: Mario Maker coin milestone 0 at 6871 points vs requires 10

adjacentRowRequiresRatio.evidence: 54 sane samples; anti-pattern A1 = ratio below 1 (The Click Tree 100000→50→30→20→10→5)

prestigeExponentByRow.evidence: corpus histogram: exponent 0.5 in 179 layers, deeper rows drift 0.4→0.1

upgradeCostRatioChained.evidence: 2674 samples; two regimes: gentle 5-upgrade ladders and aggressive row-end jumps

upgradeGrid.idScheme: row-column ids: 11,12,13,14,15,21,... (first upgrade costs ~0–1; last column's final upgrade = 'unlock a new layer' exit ticket)

milestonesPerLayer.densityFloor: at least 3–5 per main layer (anti-pattern A4: thin layers)

milestoneThresholdSpacing.source: 09 §4 row 8; P17 (the threshold number IS the design)

base.note: base 2 = next purchase always ~1 reset away; 5–10 = hard spending decisions

staticLayer.semantic: static layers are 'buy N times' counters; canBuyMax() gated by an upgrade is the standard reward

buyableCostCurve.costSoftcap: optional: blunt late scaling after ~25 purchases (cost-softcap idiom, 01 §7)

softcap.startAt: approximately where the NEXT layer unlocks
softcap.hardCap: power 0 — softcap(value, cap, 0) freezes the value; use for theme ceilings (exam score 150)
softcap.defenseInDepth: three independent places (P12): (1) layer softcap/softcapPower props, (2) softcap() helper inside individual effect()s, (3) staged re-root ladders in custom getResetGain()

automationLadder.crossLayerGrants: layer N's milestones automate layers < N; achievements are an alternate path (P11, with !has guards)
automationLadder.antiPattern: A8 — never one milestone grants everything; one chore removed per step

hotkeyCoverage.rule: every resettable layer gets a hotkey

currencyRetention.rule: each new layer adds at least one gainMult() line to at least TWO older layers, and at least one of its upgrades boosts the FIRST layer
currencyRetention.antiPattern: A7 orphaned first layer; test: 'does layer 1 upgrade 11 still matter at endgame?'

layerDensity.evidence: high-rated games: ~15 (Mining) to ~27 (Mario Maker 2) content items per main layer; low-rated: ~5–7

authorPacingTargets._source: references/design/12-Author-Design-Wisdom.md — design notes by Acamaeda (the TMT author), 2020-10..2023-04. These outrank the corpus statistics where they disagree.
authorPacingTargets.firstBoostNote: It should not take more than 10 seconds to get the very first boost in the game (2021-05-20). Enforced in practice by keeping the row-0 first upgrade at cost ~1.

firstUpgradeCost.note: Combined with base gain new Decimal(1)/sec this lands the first purchase inside the 10s budget.

authorPacingTargets.minimumGainPerReset: if a reset cycle runs longer than a minute, EVERY reset must pay something — more currency carried in, or a new purchase (2020-10-07)
authorPacingTargets.resetSpeedup: a major reset must speed the game up from the first second, not after automation comes online (2020-10-07)
authorPacingTargets.resetBudgetTarget: each new layer gets the player to the point of the next one, then visibly slows there (2020-10-07)
authorPacingTargets.costScalingOverSoftcap: cost scaling is the primary shaping tool; softcaps only where a loop would truly run away, because a softcapped x10 reads as less than x10 to the player (2022-07-04)
authorPacingTargets.softcapUpgradeRequiresVisibility: only sell a cap-raising upgrade if the cap is visible to the player (2021-02-24)
authorPacingTargets.staticCurrencyNeedsBuyMaxEarly: static currencies require unlockable buy-max early, or the loop is a thousand identical clicks (2020-10-07)
authorPacingTargets.scaleAtZero: an upgrade that scales with the currency spent must still give a real bonus at zero (2020-10-07)
authorPacingTargets.exponentNotForEarly: exponents are weak on small values and make bad early upgrades; use flat/absolute bonuses in the first layer (2020-10-07)
authorPacingTargets.hardResetForbidden: never hard reset the player — not for cheating, not for inflation (use fixOldSaves) (2020-10-07)
authorPacingTargets.gatesByThreshold: never gate a paid layer behind a purchase; use a milestone / requires / display-text threshold (2022-06-26)
authorPacingTargets.unlockAlongsideFeatures: reveal upgrades alongside new features, never one at a time (2022-07-03)
authorPacingTargets.productionVsQoLSplit: never force a choice between production and QOL from one static pool — separate sources, orderable upgrades, or a tech tree (2021-02-24)
authorPacingTargets.maxEffectsNote: one production bonus per upgrade; 3+ effects is never needed (2021-02-24). Two is allowed only across genuinely distinct resources.
authorPacingTargets.noMetaUpgrades: never boost another upgrade's effect; boost resources or named mechanics instead (2021-02-24) — narrows effect-kind K4
authorPacingTargets.milestonesVsAchievements: past ~15 milestones per layer, prefer achievements — they are more compact and easier to reach back through (2021-09-09)
authorPacingTargets.staticLayerAutomation: automate static layers with resetsNothing + autoPrestige; normal layers with passiveGeneration (2020-10-07)
authorPacingTargets.automationDefaultsOn: set toggleable automation true when it unlocks; most players would rather have it running (2022-09-27)
authorPacingTargets.displaySpentCurrency: if a tab spends a currency often, display that currency in the tab (2022-07-05)
authorPacingTargets.noInternalNames: never show buyable ids, prestige exponents, upgrade ids or the raw points name to the player (2021-02-24)
authorPacingTargets.noArrowFunctions: never use () => for layer/component functions — they have no own `this` (2020-10-07). Static rule N-ARROWTHIS.
authorPacingTargets.expantaNumProhibited: ExpantaNum/TMT+ performs badly and is unsupported until you exceed Break_Eternity (1.8e308 e's) — use Decimal (2021-05-20)

whenDefaultsMustMove.themeWithNaturalCeilings: hard-cap via softcap(x, cap, 0) and stop that currency's ladder at the cap (Gaokao: exam score 150)
whenDefaultsMustMove.idleFirstAudience: prefer log/custom gains (P8b) over sqrt resets; lengthen the automation ladder
whenDefaultsMustMove.shortGameScope: small tree + dense milestones beats many thin layers (A4)
